metadata.title: [FEATURE]: Implement upstream MCP session persistence for stateful servers (Playwright, etc.)
metadata.author: EimantasPelikis

description:

### 🧭 Epic

**Title:** MCP Session Persistence for Stateful Servers

**Goal:** Enable stateful MCP servers (e.g., Playwright browser automation) to maintain session continuity across multiple tool invocations by reusing upstream MCP client connections instead of creating new sessions for each tool call.

**Why now:** Currently, multi-step workflows with stateful MCP servers fail because element references, browser contexts, and other session-scoped state are lost between tool calls. This breaks critical use cases like browser automation, database transactions, and any workflow requiring state persistence. Users cannot perform basic multi-step operations like "navigate to page, then click button" without encountering "element not found" errors.

---

### 🧑🏻‍💻 User Story 1

**As a:** Developer using Playwright MCP server for browser automation

**I want:** Element references captured in one tool call to remain valid in subsequent tool calls

**So that:** I can perform multi-step browser workflows like "navigate to page, capture element, click element" without the element reference becoming invalid

#### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Multi-step browser automation workflow
  Given I have a gateway session connected to a Playwright MCP server
  When I call browser_navigate and capture element ref "e23"
  And I call browser_click with ref "e23" in the same gateway session
  Then the click succeeds without "ref not found" errors
  And both tool calls use the same upstream Playwright session ID

Scenario: Session isolation between different users
  Given User A has gateway session "session-a"
  And User B has gateway session "session-b"
  When User A navigates to page X and captures element ref "e1"
  And User B navigates to page Y and captures element ref "e2"
  Then User A's ref "e1" is only valid in session "session-a"
  And User B's ref "e2" is only valid in session "session-b"
  And there is no state leakage between sessions
```

---

### 🧑🏻‍💻 User Story 2

**As a:** Platform operator monitoring gateway performance

**I want:** Upstream MCP sessions to be reused across tool calls within the same gateway session

**So that:** I can reduce connection overhead, improve latency, and see clear metrics on session reuse rates

#### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Session reuse reduces latency
  Given I have a gateway session with multiple tool calls
  When I invoke the first tool (creates new upstream session)
  And I invoke the second tool (reuses existing upstream session)
  Then the second tool call has lower latency (no initialize overhead)
  And metrics show session_reuses_total incremented
  And metrics show session_creates_total only incremented once

Scenario: Idle session cleanup
  Given I have an upstream session that has been idle for 5 minutes
  When the idle timeout expires
  Then the upstream session is evicted from the registry
  And metrics show session_evictions_total{reason="idle"} incremented
  And the next tool call creates a fresh upstream session
```

---

### 🧑🏻‍💻 User Story 3

**As a:** Developer building stateful workflows with any MCP server

**I want:** The gateway to automatically maintain upstream session continuity

**So that:** I don't need to manually manage session IDs or worry about connection lifecycle

#### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Transparent session management
  Given I am using any stateful MCP server (Playwright, database, etc.)
  When I make multiple tool calls in the same gateway session
  Then the gateway automatically binds my gateway session to one upstream session
  And I never see session ID mismatches in logs
  And session cleanup happens automatically when I close my gateway session

Scenario: Session recovery on upstream failure
  Given I have an active upstream session
  When the upstream MCP server restarts or becomes unhealthy
  And I make another tool call
  Then the gateway detects the broken session via health check
  And automatically creates a new upstream session
  And my tool call succeeds (with fresh state)
```

---

### 📐 Design Sketch

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Gateway
    participant Registry as Upstream Session Registry
    participant Playwright as Playwright MCP Server

    Note over Client,Playwright: First Tool Call (browser_navigate)
    Client->>Gateway: POST /servers/:ID/mcp (MCP-Session-Id: gateway-123)
    Gateway->>Registry: acquire(downstream_id="gateway-123", url="http://playwright:8000")
    Registry->>Playwright: Initialize new session
    Playwright-->>Registry: Session ID: upstream-abc
    Registry-->>Gateway: Return session handle
    Gateway->>Playwright: tools/call browser_navigate (session: upstream-abc)
    Playwright-->>Gateway: Success, element ref "e23"
    Gateway-->>Client: Success

    Note over Client,Playwright: Second Tool Call (browser_click)
    Client->>Gateway: POST /servers/:ID/mcp (MCP-Session-Id: gateway-123)
    Gateway->>Registry: acquire(downstream_id="gateway-123", url="http://playwright:8000")
    Registry-->>Gateway: Return SAME session handle (upstream-abc)
    Gateway->>Playwright: tools/call browser_click ref="e23" (session: upstream-abc)
    Playwright-->>Gateway: Success (ref valid in same session)
    Gateway-->>Client: Success

    Note over Client,Playwright: Session Cleanup
    Client->>Gateway: DELETE /servers/:ID/mcp (MCP-Session-Id: gateway-123)
    Gateway->>Registry: evict_downstream_session("gateway-123")
    Registry->>Playwright: Close session upstream-abc
    Gateway-->>Client: 200 OK
```

**Key Components:**

1. **Upstream Session Registry** (`mcpgateway/services/upstream_session_registry.py`):
   - Already exists, provides 1:1 downstream→upstream session binding
   - Handles session lifecycle, health checks, and eviction

2. **Tool Service Integration** (`mcpgateway/services/tool_service.py`):
   - Currently creates ad-hoc connections (PROBLEM)
   - Needs to use registry.acquire() instead (SOLUTION)

3. **Session Cleanup Hook** (`mcpgateway/transports/streamablehttp_transport.py`):
   - Trigger registry.evict_downstream_session() on DELETE /mcp

---

### 🔗 MCP Standards Check

- [x] Change adheres to current [MCP specifications](https://developer.ibm.com/tutorials/awb-handle-remote-tool-calling-model-context-protocol/)
- [x] No breaking changes to existing MCP-compliant integrations
- [ ] If deviations exist, please describe them below:

**Standards Compliance:**
- MCP protocol defines session lifecycle via initialize/close
- This enhancement maintains protocol compliance by properly managing session lifecycle
- Existing stateless MCP servers continue to work unchanged
- Session reuse is transparent to MCP clients (no protocol changes)

---

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

1. **Client-side session management:**
   - Rejected: Puts burden on every client to track upstream session IDs
   - Rejected: Breaks abstraction layer provided by gateway

2. **Sticky routing at load balancer level:**
   - Rejected: Only solves worker affinity, not upstream session reuse
   - Rejected: Doesn't help single-worker deployments

3. **Stateless-only MCP servers:**
   - Rejected: Eliminates entire class of valuable use cases (browser automation, transactions, etc.)
   - Rejected: MCP protocol explicitly supports stateful sessions

4. **Manual session ID passing in tool arguments:**
   - Rejected: Violates MCP protocol (session ID is transport-level, not tool-level)
   - Rejected: Breaks existing tools and clients

**Chosen Solution:**
Integrate existing upstream session registry into tool service invocation path. This:
- ✅ Maintains protocol compliance
- ✅ Requires no client changes
- ✅ Leverages existing infrastructure
- ✅ Provides transparent session management

---

**Evidence from Production Logs:**
```
First Tool Call:
  Gateway Session:    9f8e4a37d3f9405f8b1a27cdeba39c9b
  Playwright Session: 4b444be5-b907-45e1-8cba-faf14c470231
  Result: ✓ Successfully navigated, captured element ref e23

Second Tool Call:
  Gateway Session:    9f8e4a37d3f9405f8b1a27cdeba39c9b (SAME ✓)
  Playwright Session: 7a3681dc-6897-45c4-a802-61c73869656c (DIFFERENT ✗)
  Result: ✗ Error - Ref e23 not found in current page snapshot
```

**Impact:**
- **High Priority:** Blocks all multi-step stateful workflows
- **User-Facing:** Directly impacts developer experience with browser automation
- **Technical Debt:** Existing infrastructure (registry) is unused, creating maintenance burden

**Success Metrics:**
- Session reuse rate > 90% for multi-call workflows
- Latency improvement for subsequent calls (no initialize overhead)
- Zero "element not found" errors in multi-step Playwright workflows
- Memory usage remains bounded (idle eviction works)
